title: Console UX notes: Quality Gate results + override flow (wire notes)
content:
Context / goal
- We’re adding mandatory Quality Gates before Optimize config recommendations can be applied (one-click or auto-apply). Console needs to clearly communicate:
  1) current gate status + why
  2) what changed (config diff) + what baseline it was compared against
  3) meaningful quality deltas (pass/fail + details)
  4) where to inspect artifacts
  5) how to request / grant overrides with strong friction + audit trail

Users + primary questions
- Optimize user (self-serve dev): “Can I apply this change safely? If not, what do I do next?”
- Applied ML / Evals: “What metrics moved? Is this real regression or flake?”
- SRE/oncall: “Is gate system healthy? Is this a widespread issue? Should we halt rollouts?”
- Enterprise admin / approver: “What evidence supports an override? What’s the time bound and blast radius?”

Entry points (where gate results show up)
1) Optimize Recommendation details drawer / page
- In the list of recommendations, each item has a small status chip (Passed / Failed / Running / Requires override / Not run).
- Clicking a recommendation opens a details panel: Summary header + tabs (Overview, Results, Artifacts, Audit).

2) Rollout / Change page (if we represent applying the config as a change object)
- A “Quality Gate” section in the change sidebar.
- If the rollout controller blocks promotion, the UI needs to point to the specific gate run that blocked it.

3) Route / Model configuration page
- If a user attempts manual config edits that are in-scope, UI intercepts and enforces the same gate UX (or at minimum logs + points to gating).

Core UI model: Gate Run
- A Gate Run is a concrete evaluation of a specific proposed config diff compared to a selected baseline.
- Gate results are immutable; multiple gate runs may exist for the same recommendation (re-run, new prompt set version, new baseline).
- UI should always surface “latest run” + ability to switch to previous runs.

Status model (chips + colors, wire semantics)
- Pending (not scheduled yet)
- Running (with progress + time estimate)
- Passed
- Failed
- Inconclusive / Flaky (special case; see below)
- Overridden (gate failed but override granted)
- Expired (override expired; action required)
- Canceled (by user/system)

Header summary (Recommendation details)
- Left: Recommendation title + route/model
  - Example: “Optimize: switch quant profile to q4_kv for llama-3.1-70b / A100-80GB (route: /v1/chat/completions)”
- Right: Primary CTA area depending on status
  - Passed: [Apply change] (or [Start rollout])
  - Running: [View progress] + [Cancel]
  - Failed: [View failures] + [Request override]
  - Overridden: [Apply change] (with warning + expiration date)

Top-line quality verdict component (always visible)
- One sentence summary + small metric highlights.
- Copy examples:
  - Passed: “Quality gate passed. No statistically significant regression detected vs baseline.”
  - Failed: “Quality gate failed. Regression detected on 2/6 required metrics (Task success, Safety rubric).”
  - Flaky/Inconclusive: “Gate inconclusive due to high variance. Rerun recommended (auto-rerun scheduled).”

Key metadata in summary block
- Gate run ID (copyable)
- Gate tier: Smoke vs Full (and why this tier was chosen)
- Baseline: “Current production config” OR “Pinned baseline: profile=q8_0, batching=v2”
- Prompt set / suite version: “optimize-gating-core@2025-12-01”
- Started at, finished at, eval region
- Compute cost (optional but useful for internal): “~$18.40” + runtime “17m 22s”

Results tab: Metric table (comparison view)
- Core pattern: baseline value, candidate value, delta, threshold, verdict.
- Table columns (first wire):
  - Metric name (with tooltip definition)
  - Baseline
  - Candidate
  - Δ (absolute and/or %)
  - Gate threshold / allowed regression
  - Confidence / sample size
  - Status icon
- Provide a toggle: “Show only failing metrics”
- Provide a filter by suite/prompt category (e.g., long-context, tool-use, coding, safety)

Metric row behavior
- Clicking a metric expands:
  - distribution plot thumbnail (if we have it)
  - top regressions examples (links to specific prompts)
  - “Why failed” text (from eval harness) + recommended next step
- If we can’t render charts initially, show:
  - “p95 delta”, “n=XXX prompts”, “reruns=Y”, “flake score” as text

Prompt-level drilldown (artifact-driven)
- A separate “Examples” subpanel for failing prompts:
  - Prompt ID
  - Category tag(s)
  - Baseline output snippet + candidate output snippet (diff view)
  - Score details (rubric + model grader output if applicable)
  - Link: “Open full artifact” (to eval harness artifact store)

Artifacts tab: Make it boring + linkable
- Provide canonical links to:
  - Run summary JSON
  - Per-prompt results CSV/JSONL
  - HTML report (if generated)
  - Logs (eval harness job logs)
  - Config diff payload (what Optimize sent)
- Display as a list with: name, created timestamp, “copy link” icon.
- Add a “Sensitive data” warning if artifacts may include customer prompts (depends on account tier / anonymization). If we do anonymization, note it explicitly.

Config Diff panel (inline in Overview tab)
- Always show proposed change in a structured way (not raw JSON first).
- Sections by knob type:
  - Batching policy
  - KV/prefix caching
  - Quantization profile
- Show “before → after” with a short explanation line from Optimize recommendation engine.
- Provide “View raw diff” (read-only) for debugging.

Gate tier UX: Smoke vs Full
- Smoke gate should show as “Fast check” not “partial/less safe” (avoid undermining trust).
- Copy suggestion:
  - “Fast check passed. Full evaluation required before production rollout.”
  - “Full evaluation passed. Safe to roll out per policy.”
- UI should show required next step when smoke passes:
  - CTA: [Run full gate] (if not auto-triggered)
  - OR automatically schedule and show “Full evaluation scheduled”

Running state UX
- Show progress steps (even if approximate):
  1) Validating config diff
  2) Selecting baseline
  3) Scheduling eval jobs
  4) Running suites (X/Y)
  5) Aggregating results
- If we have suite-level progress, show a checklist with live updates.
- If running exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30m), show a banner:
  - “Longer than usual. This may be due to GPU scarcity in region. You can cancel and retry in another region.” (if supported)

Failure states UX (what to do next)
- Distinguish between:
  A) True quality regression
  B) System failure (timeouts, infra errors)
  C) Inconclusive / flaky

A) Quality regression
- Banner content:
  - “Regression detected. Apply blocked by policy.”
  - Link: “View failing metrics”
  - Secondary CTA: [Rerun gate] (if allowed)
  - Secondary CTA: [Request override]

B) System failure
- Banner content:
  - “Evaluation could not be completed (timeout / infra error). Apply blocked.”
  - Provide reason code + incident link if exists
  - CTA: [Retry] + “Try different region” if available

C) Flaky/Inconclusive
- Banner content:
  - “Inconclusive due to high variance; auto-rerun scheduled in ~10m.”
  - CTA: [Rerun now]
  - Show flake score and how it’s calculated (tooltip)
  - Note: avoid presenting inconclusive as pass.

Override flow (request → approve → apply)
- Strong principle: override is time-bound, scoped, and auditable.

Where override lives in UI
- In Failed state header, show [Request override].
- If user lacks permission, show disabled button + “Contact an admin” tooltip.

Override request modal (wire copy)
- Title: “Request quality gate override”
- Warning text (red): “This change failed quality checks and may regress outputs in production.”
- Required fields:
  - Justification (textarea) with prompt: “Why is this safe/necessary?”
  - Risk acceptance checkbox: “I understand this may degrade responses and will monitor impact.”
  - Desired expiration (dropdown): 4h / 24h / 72h / custom (policy-limited)
  - Scope (if policy supports): “This route only” vs “Account-wide” (default narrow)
  - Links/evidence (optional): paste links to artifacts, prior incidents, customer approval
- After submission:
  - state becomes “Override requested”
  - show who can approve (role or names) and expected SLA

Override requested state (in recommendation)
- Status chip: “Override requested”
- Banner: “Awaiting approval from <role>. Apply remains blocked.”
- Show request details (who requested, when, justification, expiration requested).

Override granted state
- Status chip: “Overridden (expires <date>)”
- Banner (yellow): “Override granted by <name>. Expires <date>. This apply will be recorded in audit logs.”
- Primary CTA: [Apply change]
- Secondary CTA: [Run full gate again] (encouraged)

Override denial
- Status: “Override denied” (don’t keep this forever; might roll into the audit tab)
- Banner: “Denied by <name> — <reason>”
- CTA: [Rerun gate] / [Edit recommendation] (if possible) / [Contact support]

Audit tab (must-have for enterprise / internal)
- Timeline feed:
  - Gate triggered (who/what triggered it: auto from Optimize, manual user action)
  - Gate completed + result
  - Rerun(s)
  - Override requested + details
  - Override granted/denied + approver + expiration
  - Apply attempted (blocked) / apply succeeded
  - Rollout started / canary promotion blocked / rollback triggered
- Each event should have:
  - timestamp
  - actor (user/service)
  - route/model/config identifiers
  - link to run/artifact

Copy tone notes
- Avoid jargon like “p-value” in top-line summary; keep stats in expanded details.
- Use “Blocked” instead of “Not allowed” to reduce blame.
- Always provide a next step: view failures, rerun, request override.

RBAC / permissions notes (needs alignment w/ PM-482)
- Suggest roles:
  - Request override: route owner, oncall, PM
  - Approve override: enterprise admin (customer side) + Redwood oncall (internal) depending on deployment mode
- UI must show “You don’t have permission” + who to contact.

Open questions / TODOs (for next pass)
1) Do we show “Apply change” on recommendation page, or route through Rollouts flow always?
2) What is the canonical object: Recommendation, Config Change, or Gate Run? (Impacts breadcrumbs + deep links)
3) Baseline selection: how to explain baseline when it’s not current prod (e.g., per GPU SKU quant baseline)?
4) What’s the right level of detail for self-serve vs enterprise?
   - Potential: “Simple view” vs “Advanced view” toggle.
5) Handling multiple prompt sets / suites:
   - Do we aggregate into one verdict or show per-suite verdict chips?
6) Artifact link privacy:
   - For customer prompts, do we redact by default? If so, what do we show in the UI for prompt-level diffs?
7) Flaky suite quarantine:
   - If a suite is quarantined mid-run, what’s the UI state? “Partial results” vs “Inconclusive”?

Wire sketch notes (text-only)
- Recommendation details layout
  - Header row: [Back] Recommendation title | Status chip | Primary CTA
  - Row 2: Gate summary (verdict, tier, baseline, suite version)
  - Tabs: Overview | Results | Artifacts | Audit

- Results tab
  - Left: Metric table (sortable)
  - Right: Expand panel for selected metric (examples + distribution)

- Artifacts tab
  - List with names + copy link + open
  - At bottom: “Need help reproducing?” → link to runbook / docs

Proposed minimal MVP for Console (aligns with ENG-3925)
- Must ship:
  - Gate status chip + block apply messaging
  - Summary verdict component (pass/fail/running)
  - Link to artifacts (at least run summary + logs)
  - Basic metrics table with failing metrics highlighted
  - Override request + show override granted/expired state (even if approvals happen outside Console v0)
- Nice-to-have:
  - Prompt-level diffs rendered inline
  - Charts/distributions
  - Suite-level progress UI

Notes from quick review (2025-12-05)
- Aditya: keep the “safe-by-default” story. Don’t make override feel like a normal path.
- Jonas: must show sample size + rerun count somewhere, otherwise we’ll get endless Slack questions.
- Jordan: enforcement is defense-in-depth; UI should never imply you can bypass gating via direct API.

Next steps
- Sync with Kenji/Alicia on copy + component spec for status chips and banners.
- Confirm data contract for what Console gets back from Optimize (needed fields for summary + artifact links).
- Draft v0 screens in Figma (DES-611) based on these notes; review w/ PM-482 for override UX + policy constraints.
